score_evidence.A: Two heading-only H2 sections duplicated by the next H2: L299 '## 하드웨어 백엔드별 설치: CUDA, ROCm, TPU, Apple Silicon, CPU' followed directly by L302 '## 하드웨어 백엔드마다 다른 설치 경로와 따로 받는 커널'; L610 '## vLLM 선택 기준: ...' followed directly by L613 '## 동시 요청이 많을수록 커지는 vLLM의 이점과 그 한계'. Front matter, $$ math, 40 paired fences and real tables are fine.
score_evidence.B: Formulaic frames repeat: L83 '숫자로 따라가 보면 이렇습니다.', L172 '숫자를 넣어 보면 절감 규모를 가늠할 수 있습니다.', L268 '구체적인 숫자로 따라가 보면 동작이 잘 보입니다.' Terminology drifts between '반복' (L248-276) and 'iteration' (L490 '한 iteration에', L517 'iteration당'). Repeated '서드파티인 X 글은' attribution (L51, L65, L109, L137, L139) reads mechanically. Register is consistent '입니다'.
score_evidence.C: Running example used before it is introduced: L133 '이 글의 실행 예시 모델도' and L193 '실행 예시의 채팅 서버에서는' come before the model is first named (L172) and before any server is started (L344/L462). L268 '토큰 상한을 앞서 든 예시값으로 두고' refers to an example value never given (L256 defines the flag without a value). L115 '앞서 소개한 PagedAttention 논문' although the paper was never introduced. The OS analogy is restated verbatim at L49 and L103 ('블록은 페이지, 토큰은 바이트, 시퀀스는 프로세스').
score_evidence.D: Good help where it is hard: block-wise attention formula with symbol glossary and B=4 worked example (L79-83), block-table table (L121-127), CoW trace (L174-181), chunked-prefill trace (L270-276). Some padding on version disputes (L293 third-party disagreement on default preemption mode).
score_evidence.E: Useful tables/code/figures, but L634 image is the blog's perf_a100_n3_light.png (three parallel outputs, A100 only) while the alt text and L632 say '요청당 출력 1개일 때 A100과 A10G'. Three images hot-link the vllm.ai host (L107, L170, L634).
score_evidence.F: Two wrong claims in the sample (figure caption L632/L634; stale metric name vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc L540/L554, renamed vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc in current vLLM). L499 current-docs cell '기존 50%가 다른 vLLM 인스턴스의 몫이면 ... 이 인스턴스의 한도는 GPU 메모리의 90%' is the writer's inference presented as a docs table cell. L15/L260 '청크 단위 프리필을 켜면' implies off by default; SchedulerConfig.enable_chunked_prefill defaults to True.
score_evidence.T1: Install commands match docs and would run. But: no request to the running server is ever shown (no curl or OpenAI-client call, though L453 heading promises 'OpenAI 클라이언트가 그대로 붙는'); the config-file subsection (L482-486) shows neither a YAML example nor the --config flag; offline script (L426-439) never prints outputs; metrics script watches a metric current vLLM no longer emits; HPA snippet L599 drops the keda: parent the docs nest it under.
score_evidence.T2: Covers the sources' main topics in a sensible order (problem, PagedAttention, allocation, sharing, architecture, scheduler, install, offline, serve, tuning, metrics, autoscaling, choice). Some padding from v0.6.4/v0.7.3 material (L240, L293, L527).
score_evidence.T3: Strong internals (kernel fusion, block pool, slot mapping, prefix-cache eviction, TP broadcast, AsyncLLM/EngineCore split) and system fit (metrics, KEDA, scale-to-zero). Old-version material is labelled by version. Failure modes are partly covered (preemption, batch-1, NUMA OOM, FP8 scaling); no startup/OOM troubleshooting.

examples.claim: existing systems waste 60-80% of KV memory; PagedAttention waste under 4%
examples.source: blog.vllm.ai 2023-06-20: 'existing systems waste 60% – 80% of memory due to fragmentation and over-reservation' ... 'a mere waste of under 4%'

examples.claim: OPT-13B KV per token = 2 x 5120 x 40 x 2 bytes ~ 800 KB
examples.source: arXiv 2309.06180 §3: 'the KV cache of a single token demands 800 KB of space, calculated as 2 (key and value vectors) × 5120 (hidden state size) × 40 (number of layers) × 2 (bytes per FP16)'

examples.claim: block table entry holds the physical block and number of filled positions
examples.source: paper §4.3: 'Each block table entry records the corresponding physical blocks of a logical block and the number of filled positions.'
paper §7.2: 'Accordingly, vLLM sets its default block size as 16.'

examples.claim: memory sharing cuts parallel-sampling/beam-search memory up to 55%, throughput up to 2.2x
examples.source: blog: 'cutting their memory usage by up to 55%. This can translate into up to 2.2x improvement in throughput.'
